headline: Anthropic releases Opus 5.5 with Fable-level performance at lower prices
summary: Anthropic's newest AI model, Opus 5.5, offers significant performance gains and a 20% price reduction for output tokens compared to its predecessor.
details: Anthropic has launched Opus 5.5, its most capable AI model, boasting performance that rivals and in some cases surpasses the larger Fable model. This new iteration is also notably cheaper, with output tokens priced at $20 per million, a reduction from the previous $25.

The company states that Opus 5.5 excels in coding and knowledge work, outperforming Fable in various benchmarks and informal tasks. The model also features improved communication, using less jargon and prioritizing key information at the beginning of its responses.

This release follows closely on the heels of Opus 5, launched just two months prior. Anthropic also announced that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, the other tiers in their Claude lineup, are expected in the coming weeks with similar performance enhancements.

Opus 5.5 incorporates enhanced safety measures, comparable to those for the Fable model, restricting its use in sensitive areas like developing biological weapons or discovering exploits in compiled programs. This aligns with CEO Dario Amodei's recent emphasis on pacing AI capabilities to match alignment progress.

Anthropic is investing in advanced training and evaluation systems for future models, including improved security and monitoring. The company believes public policy will play a crucial role in ensuring the safety of AI systems as they become more powerful.
caption:
Anthropic's Opus 5.5 AI model is here, outperforming Fable and slashing prices by 20%.

Anthropic has launched Opus 5.5, its most capable AI model, boasting performance that rivals and in some cases surpasses the larger Fable model. This new iteration is also notably cheaper, with output tokens priced at $20 per million, a reduction from the previous $25.

The company states that Opus 5.5 excels in coding and knowledge work, outperforming Fable in various benchmarks and informal tasks. The model also features improved communication, using less jargon and prioritizing key information at the beginning of its responses.

This release follows closely on the heels of Opus 5, launched just two months prior. Anthropic also announced that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, the other tiers in their Claude lineup, are expected in the coming weeks with similar performance enhancements.

Opus 5.5 incorporates enhanced safety measures, comparable to those for the Fable model, restricting its use in sensitive areas like developing biological weapons or discovering exploits in compiled programs. This aligns with CEO Dario Amodei's recent emphasis on pacing AI capabilities to match alignment progress.

Anthropic is investing in advanced training and evaluation systems for future models, including improved security and monitoring. The company believes public policy will play a crucial role in ensuring the safety of AI systems as they become more powerful.
